answer: The mechanism, called comet-random quill signing, requires each agent to answer a hash-challenge drawn from a public verifiable randomness beacon before its identity is registered. An attacker cannot precompute thousands of identities because each quill must bind to a fresh comet output that is unpredictable before the beacon publishes. The per-identity cost is one umber token burned into the beacon log, which rises linearly with every additional identity an attacker tries to register in the same round.
